problem: Goal-conditioned visual navigation methods either map observations directly to actions (poor adaptation to novel environments) or pair a planner with a separately trained world model, which causes state-action misalignment and compounding errors over long horizons because trajectory memory is absent.
motivation: Effective navigation requires imagining the outcomes of actions while acting, and remembering past context over time. Modular planner + world model pipelines (e.g., NWM) learn prediction and control in isolation, and unified autoregressive models still drift over long horizons without temporal structure.
key_idea: Use a single multimodal autoregressive backbone (Anole-7B) that alternates between predicting the next action (discretized bin tokens) and imagining the next egocentric view, augmented with a two-level (intra-step and cross-step) KV-cache memory that is fused by similarity gating and temporal decay.
insight: Joint training of planner and world model in one backbone beats separately trained versions (SR 0.71 vs 0.65), and interleaving the two substeps beats predicting both at once. Hierarchical memory gives incremental gains (e.g., Go Stanford SR 0.71 to 0.73 to 0.75; TartanDrive 0.35 to 0.38 to 0.42), but only in a few layers: 5 layers is best, while 16 or 32 layers hurt badly. Under a fixed token budget, image resolution (784 tokens with 1 context frame) matters more than more context frames.
method: Unified formulation: one MLLM F_theta alternates between action prediction a_{t+1}=F(o_t,o_s,o_g,p_0,M_t) and next-view imagination o_{t+1}=F(o_t,a_{t+1},o_s,o_g,p_0,M_t), replacing the separate planner and world model.

Multimodal tokenization: a frozen VQ image tokenizer (448x448 images give 784 tokens), a BPE tokenizer for pose and text, and a bin tokenizer that maps actions (dx, dy, dyaw) to sign-prefixed bin tokens with bin size 0.01.
Discretized bin-token loss L_plan: per-dimension classification over the bin-token sets, plus CE for text tokens such as Stop.
Reconstruction loss L_world: distance-weighted loss between the predicted visual-token distribution and the ground-truth codebook embeddings, to improve imagination fidelity.
Interleaved training: planner and world-model samples from sliding windows are mixed in the same batches. Only LoRA (rank 16) on the qkv projections is trained, with tokenizers frozen.

Hierarchical memory: the intra-step memory caches KV of the current observation span (delimited by boss/eoss tokens) at layers {0,7,15,23,31}. The cross-step memory stores past intra-step KVs with timestamps.

Spatio-temporal fusion: top-k cosine similarity gating on keys, then exponential temporal decay (gamma=0.2) normalized over the selected entries. The weighted historical KV is concatenated with the current KV and used in attention for both substeps.

setting.training_data: Go Stanford (4457 train trajectories), ReCon (4652), SCAND (2560), HuRoN (4642) for the main setting; 1X Humanoid navigation subset (6599) trained as a separate instance. TartanDrive is evaluated zero-shot.
setting.observation: Monocular egocentric RGB (start, goal and current/imagined frames) plus the initial pose p_0
setting.action_space: Continuous planar displacement (dx, dy) and yaw change, discretized into 0.01 bin tokens, plus Stop; 25-DoF joint-angle actions for the humanoid
setting.simulator: Offline real-world datasets (Go Stanford, ReCon, SCAND, HuRoN, TartanDrive, 1X Humanoid); no simulator
setting.privileged: none (initial pose p_0 and the goal image are given as inputs)

numbers.extra: Evaluation split of the preprocessed dataset (496 trajectories); success radius equals the average step size; baselines retrained on the same data

numbers_note: None of the benchmarks are among the canonical list; they are recorded as 'other:'. Split names ('val' for evaluation splits, 'test' for TartanDrive) are inferred. The paper also reports visualization metrics averaged over the four datasets: SSIM 0.457, PSNR 13.607, LPIPS 0.254, DreamSim 0.041, SSIM@5 0.350. Average over the four datasets: SR 0.78, ATE 0.32, RPE 0.12, with 82 s per trajectory.
results: UniWM outperforms retrained GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, Anole-7B and NWM on all four in-domain datasets; for example, Go Stanford SR is 0.75 vs. 0.45 for NWM, and HuRoN SR is 0.76 vs. 0.41. It generalizes zero-shot to TartanDrive (SR 0.42 vs. 0.27 for NWM) and reaches SR 0.81 on 25-DoF humanoid navigation (NWM 0.51). Imagination quality is also best, with SSIM 0.457 vs. 0.389 for NWM.
limitations: Domain shift: ego-robot parts visible in TartanDrive fade during rollouts, and a fixed token budget limits resolution and context together.
Inference is slow (about 82 s per trajectory vs. 0.6 s for NoMaD), and the 4-bit quantization speed (16 s) is only estimated.
Evaluation is offline on datasets with no closed-loop or real-robot deployment; the humanoid case needs a separate model per action space.
